source.place: Section 4, Sub-lemma 4.5, trivial-cofibration arrow-category argument; Section 3, enriched model axiom; Section 6, Lemma 6.2, saturated subcategory restriction. Read online; not archived locally. No Stacks tag supplies this dg-category statement.

proof.text: For objects $c:P\to Q$ and $c':P'\to Q'$, a homogeneous element of degree $r$ in the displayed pullback is a pair $(a,b)$ with $c'a=bc$. Because $c,c'$ are closed and of degree zero, $c'\,d(a)=d(b)c$, so the pullback is a subcomplex. If $(a',b')$ is another composable homogeneous square, then $c''a'a=b'c'a=b'bc$, so componentwise composition remains in the pullback. Associativity, units $(1_P,1_Q)$, and the differential Leibniz rule are inherited componentwise from $\mathcal M$. Thus this is a dg category, and its two projections are dg functors to the full dg subcategory on cofibrant objects of $\mathcal S$.

source.place: Section 4, proof of Sub-lemma 4.5, pp. 20–21, trivial-cofibration case; elementary expansion by Q22.

proof.text:
Let $*$ be a terminal object of $\mathcal M$. The ordinary morphisms are the degree-zero cycles, so the unique endomorphism of $*$ is both its identity and zero. For every homogeneous morphism into or out of $*$, composition with this zero identity equals both that morphism and zero. Thus all complexes involving $*$ vanish. For $c:P\to Q$ and $c':P'\to Q'$, apply the enriched model axiom to the trivial cofibration $c$ and the fibration $Q'\to *$; the latter is a fibration because every object is fibrant. The two terminal Hom complexes vanish, so the resulting map is precisely
$$\rho=c^*:\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Q')\longrightarrow\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Q').$$
It is a degreewise surjective quasi-isomorphism. Here the weak equivalence required by the axiom is $c$, not $Q'\to *$.

source.place: Section 4, proof of Sub-lemma 4.5, pp. 20–21, trivial-cofibration case; elementary expansion by Q22.

proof.text: In the model structure on $\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$ from the cited enriched-model statement, $\rho$ is therefore a trivial fibration. The map on Hom complexes induced by $e_0$ is its pullback along $c'_*:\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,P')\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Q')$. To check its right lifting property against any cofibration $j:U\to V$ of complexes, take a lifting square for the pullback projection. Its $B=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Q')$ component and the composite $V\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,P')\to\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Q')$ form a lifting square for $\rho$ against $j$. A lift $V\to B$ pairs with the prescribed map from $V$ to the other factor, giving a lift into the pullback. The weak factorization system (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) identifies this projection as a trivial fibration. Since fibrations of complexes are degreewise surjections and weak equivalences are quasi-isomorphisms, every Hom map of $e_0$ has the claimed two properties.

source.place: Section 4, proof of Sub-lemma 4.5, pp. 20–21, trivial-cofibration case; elementary expansion by Q22.

proof.text: For every cofibrant $X\in\mathcal S$, the identity $1_X$ is a trivial cofibration with both endpoints $X$, so it is an object of $\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$. Sending $X$ to $1_X$ and a homogeneous morphism $a$ to $(a,a)$ defines a dg functor $s$; the pullback relation, differential, composition and units are preserved componentwise. It satisfies $e_0s=e_1s=1$ strictly. In particular $e_0$ is surjective on objects. Together with step 3 this makes $e_0$ a quasi-equivalence: its Hom maps are quasi-isomorphisms and its $H^0$ functor is essentially surjective.

source.place: Section 4, proof of Sub-lemma 4.5, pp. 20–21, trivial-cofibration case; elementary expansion by Q22.

proof.text: Quasi-equivalences are the weak equivalences of the cited dg-category model structure, hence satisfy two-out-of-three. Apply this first to $s$ followed by $e_0$: both $e_0$ and $e_0s=1$ are weak equivalences, so $s$ is one. Apply it next to $s$ followed by $e_1$: both $s$ and $e_1s=1$ are weak equivalences, so $e_1$ is a quasi-equivalence as well. All categories are viewed in one of the sufficiently large universes allowed in the statement.

source.place: Section 4, proof of Sub-lemma 4.5, pp. 20–21, trivial-cofibration case; elementary expansion by Q22.

proof.text: In the ordinary localization $\mathsf{Hqe}$ at quasi-equivalences, $[s]$ is invertible. The strict equalities of step 4 give $[e_0][s]=[e_1][s]=1$, so cancellation yields $[e_0]=[e_1]=[s]^{-1}$. For any small dg category $\mathcal A$ and strict dg functor $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$, composition with $[T]$ gives $[e_0T]=[e_1T]$. No cofibrancy hypothesis on $\mathcal A$ is used for this equality in the ordinary localization.

source.place: Section 4, proof of Sub-lemma 4.5, pp. 20–21, trivial-cofibration case; elementary expansion by Q22.

title: Arrow dg category comparison for trivial cofibrations
statement:
Use dg categories, quasi-equivalences and $\mathsf{Hqe}$ (the ordinary localization at quasi-equivalences) as in [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure], and the complex-enriched model conventions of [lem-coef-enriched-projective-diagram-model], in universes large enough for all categories below. Let $\mathcal M$ be a category enriched over cochain complexes of abelian groups with a model structure satisfying the enriched model axiom stated there; suppose all its objects are fibrant. Let $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal M$ be a full subcategory closed under weak equivalences in both directions, and let $\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ be its full dg subcategory on cofibrant objects. Define $\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$ to have objects the trivial cofibrations $c:P\to Q$ with $P,Q$ cofibrant in $\mathcal S$, and morphism complexes
$$\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}(c,c')=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,P')\times_{\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(P,Q')}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(Q,Q'),$$
where $c':P'\to Q'$ and the maps to the middle complex are postcomposition by $c'$ and precomposition by $c$. Differential and composition are componentwise. This defines a dg category. The source projection $e_0:\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}\to\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)$ is surjective on objects and degreewise a surjective quasi-isomorphism on every morphism complex. The target projection $e_1$ is also a quasi-equivalence. The identity-arrow dg functor $s:\operatorname{Int}(\mathcal S)\to\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$ satisfies $e_0s=e_1s=1$, and $[e_0]=[e_1]$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$. Thus for any small dg category $\mathcal A$ and any strict dg functor $T:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E_{\mathcal S}$, the composites $e_0T,e_1T$ define the same morphism in $\mathsf{Hqe}$.

I checked the argument myself instead. Step 1: degree-0 closed c, c' make the pullback a subcomplex closed under composition, with no signs. Step 2: Z^0 Hom(*,*) is a singleton group, so 1_*=0 and every Hom involving * vanishes; the enriched axiom for (c, Q'->*) is valid because all objects are fibrant and c is the weak equivalence, and it gives the surjective quasi-isomorphism c^*. Step 3: I rebuilt the lift (v, l) for the pullback projection against a cofibration of complexes; it is correct. Step 4: 1_X is an isomorphism, so it is a trivial cofibration; s: a->(a,a) gives e0 s = e1 s = 1, and e0 is surjective on objects, so it is a quasi-equivalence. Steps 5-6: two-out-of-three gives s and e1, and cancellation in Hqe gives [e0]=[e1]. Edge cases checked: S empty, a zero object only, c = identity, and the strict-square sign (-1)^{r·0}=1 matching the citer's natural transformations.
